ticket: PL-14 — Wire PR #78's two dependency suites into package.json and CI
goal: Make scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs's generalized assertion ("every scripts/*.test.mjs suite has both a package.json test:* script and a matching CI step") pass on PR #83, by wiring the two suites the merge from origin/main brought in unwired — scripts/dependency-baseline.test.mjs and scripts/dependency-install.test.mjs — following the convention PL-11 used for check-lite-eligible. Amendment 1 adds one repair in the same file: the PL-12-era [inline] test's git-diff-based "these ten files are untouched" loop becomes content assertions, because as a permanent regression test it fails for any uncommitted local edit to those files (including this ticket's own) while gating nothing in CI.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `npm run test:sdd-completeness` passes, including the line-683 assertion, for all 17 scripts/*.test.mjs files currently on disk.

package.json gains exactly two scripts: test:dependency-baseline and test:dependency-install, each with the value `node --test scripts/<name>.test.mjs`. No existing key is renamed, reordered, retargeted, or removed.

.github/workflows/ci.yml gains exactly two steps in the node job, each `run: npm run <key>`, placed at the tail of the existing scripts-suite block (after "Checker read-only guard — tests", before "Pipeline control-plane scripts — typecheck"), each carrying a comment naming that the suites arrived via main unwired, that the second re-runs a real root npm ci and is slow, and that its poetry half self-skips on this runner. No existing step is reordered, renamed, or changed. Neither new step uses continue-on-error or any other non-gating modifier.
`npm run test:dependency-baseline` passes on this working tree. A failure here is a real DEPENDENCIES.md/manifest drift, to be reported (EC-3), never wired around.

Both suites are expected-green on ubuntu-latest, with the evidence stated in changes.md: (a) dependency-baseline.test.mjs performs zero spawnSync/execFileSync calls — it only reads the five workspace manifests, pyproject.toml, and DEPENDENCIES.md — so it is platform-independent, and it was green at W0-00's terminal PASS (.sdd/ledger/20260804T055818422Z-e7d473db5a-PR_DELTA-d441aa/); (b) dependency-install.test.mjs's npm half runs the same npm ci, against the same lockfile, that the job's existing "Install dependencies (root, single pass)" step already exits 0 on today, and its poetry half self-skips where poetry is absent. The known spawnSync('npm', …) ENOENT is Windows-only (npm resolves to npm.cmd, which Node will not spawn without shell: true), lives in dependency-install.test.mjs line 47 and not in the baseline suite, and does not occur on a Linux runner.

[AMENDED — A1] Nothing outside the THREE Affected files is modified (package.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs), and within the third, nothing outside the `[inline] coverage and wiring` test. (Original text: "Nothing outside the two Affected files (package.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml) is modified.")

[ADDED — A1] scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs's `[inline] coverage and wiring` test no longer asserts against `git diff --name-only HEAD`. Its ten-path loop and the adjacent `.claude/agents/**` diff check are replaced by content assertions pinning the same underlying facts — at minimum: package.json declares no inline-edit-style script (no scripts key or value naming `inline`); .github/workflows/ci.yml runs no inline-edit step (no `npm run …inline…`); scripts/tsconfig.json's file list gained no inline-edit entry; .sdd/runtimes.yml and .claude/agents/ declare no `inline-edit` agent or stage; .sdd/bounds.yml, .sdd/bounds.md, and .sdd/hotfix.md carry no inline-edit lane/bound/bypass entry; and scripts/check-lite-eligible.mjs, scripts/check-bounds.mjs, and scripts/pipeline-contracts.mjs contain no `--inline` handling. Each converted assertion must (a) pass on the current tree, (b) key on a token unique to PL-12's feature so it still fails if the thing PL-12 forbade were actually done, and (c) carry a comment recording the conversion and its reason, citing the docs/PRD_Tickets.md precedent documented immediately below it in the same test. The sibling untracked-scripts check (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard scripts`) and both docs/PRD_Tickets.md content clauses are left exactly as they are. `npm run test:sdd-completeness` must pass with PL-14's own uncommitted package.json/ci.yml edits present in the working tree — that dirty-tree pass is the proof the conversion worked, not a clean-tree run.

edgeCases.text: dependency-install's own npm ci deletes and reinstalls the root node_modules mid-job. Every later step in that job re-resolves against the fresh install, so this is safe but costs one extra install (~1–3 minutes). Stated, not discovered later.

That suite is stricter than the existing install step: findConflictLines fails on any `npm warn … peer …` / ERESOLVE line even when npm ci exits 0. Before merging, read PR #83's existing "Install dependencies (root, single pass)" log for those strings. If any appear, the wiring is still correct and the dependency graph is what needs fixing — report it as its own finding, do not weaken the step.

A dependency added since W0-00 without a DEPENDENCIES.md row makes test:dependency-baseline red. That is the suite doing its job; report it and open a separate ticket rather than editing the suite from this run (it is outside Affected files).

Running `npm run test:dependency-install` on this Windows host fails at assert.equal(result.status, 0) with status null / ENOENT. Pre-existing, platform-local, not introduced by this ticket and explicitly not fixed by it. Do not "repair" the suite here.

The poetry half never runs in CI on the node job, so the Python install path stays unexercised. Honest limit, accepted for a wiring change; the follow-up option is a second step in the python-workers job (Python 3.12 + poetry already installed there).

continue-on-error: true, or a step that runs something other than the suite, would satisfy the assertion's literal ci.includes(scriptKey) substring check while gating nothing. Rejected: a step that cannot fail is indistinguishable from no step, which is precisely the defect this assertion exists to catch.

Placement is a convention choice, not a correctness one (the assertion checks presence only). Keep the two new package.json keys and the two new CI steps in the same relative order in both files so the pairing stays obvious.

No other suite is missing wiring: all 17 scripts/*.test.mjs files are accounted for by the 15 existing test:* scripts plus these two. If a third turns up unwired at AC-1, something else landed in the same merge — report it rather than silently widening this ticket.

[ADDED — A1] Accepted residual: a content assertion cannot notice an unrelated edit to those ten files; the diff assertion could. That was never this test's job — it exists to pin what PL-12 itself must not have done, and it only had a diff available because it happened to be written during PL-12's own run. "Did this ticket touch a file it shouldn't" is owned by each ticket's own review gate and, for lane bounds, by scripts/check-bounds.mjs — not by a permanent regression suite. Also recorded plainly: the diff assertion gated nothing in CI anyway (a clean checkout diffs empty), so it only ever fired on local, in-progress trees — the opposite of where a regression gate should bite. The sibling untracked-scripts check stays git-state-based on purpose: "no new file was added" is an absence with no content to assert.
